title: Proton: NF construction, mass, charge, and computational backing
html:
Remark. Proton: NF construction, mass, charge, and computational backing

The proton definition establishes the \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d}) baryon. We derive its normal form, mass, Coulomb charge, and computational backing.

Step 1: Borromean braid NF. The inverse relation \sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_1 - h_{\mathrm{A}} \mathbf{1} yields \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0(\sigma_1 - h_{\mathrm{A}}))^3. Expanding and reducing within H_3(q) gives \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{B}_3) = +1.0000. The Hopf link terms L_\pm manifest the gluon field.

Step 2: Typed crossings. Quark flavor rigidly specifies the crossing eigenvalue. The \mathfrak{u}-\mathfrak{u} crossing preserves the eigenvalue +q. The \mathfrak{d}-type crossings impose a full -h_{\mathrm{A}} shift. Mixed \mathfrak{u}-\mathfrak{d} crossings incur a half-shift -\tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}.

LP stability constraint. (Partly withdrawn 2026-08-24.)

The bare 9-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) violates Frobenius positivity. A single Hopf link L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 is the minimum additional structure capable of restoring stability. The gluon is strictly required by the LP dual.

Those three sentences rest on \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = z^3, a weight retired on 2026-05-19 in favour of the Markov-recursion value h z^2 + z. Under the live convention the bare element has \mathrm{tr}_M = +0.544, not -0.006, and so does every intermediate step of the typed build. There is no instability for a gluon to repair, and the bare nucleon lies inside the feasible set. Whether the gluon is required on some other ground is open; the gluon ledger carries the measurement.

What survives unchanged is the scope of the enumeration. The integer LP dual enumerates all feasible gluon combinations and selects the configuration minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M|. That enumeration ranges over every non-trivial braid word inside the crossing cap, not over L_\pm alone. The trefoil word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is inside the range and is admissible; it is not selected because it loses the minimisation, not because anything forbids it (gluon ledger).

Step 3: Proton NF. Applying typed crossings and Hopf link stabilisation yields \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p}) = +1.0065. The dominant term is e^- \approx +1.022. The Hopf gluon link actively redistributes normal-form weight from \sigma_1 into the trefoil channel.

Mass. The proton mass derives from the muon-anchored Hecke energy of the Borromean braid:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} =
  2\,\bigl(\mathfrak{m}_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6\, m_e\bigr)
  + \text{Skein corrections},
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{m}_\mu = m_e\,\frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2},
  \quad
  F_{\mathrm{Bor}} = \lvert\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})\rvert\,\frac{[3]_q!}{q^3}.

The hyperbolic-volume dependence enters through the muon anchor \mathrm{Vol}(4_1), dressed by the dimensionless Borromean factor F_{\mathrm{Bor}} (computations/canonical_mass.py).

The Skein corrections isolate the crossing asymmetry between the \mathfrak{u} and \mathfrak{d} components. The pair Skein formula dictates \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}(q) + 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}}(q).
